analysis.title: Weekly Market Guide: Highly Rotational Beneath the Surface
key_insights: The S&P 500 is trading sideways and choppy, but sector, style and factor leadership is rotating quickly underneath. The index has held above key support, which the report reads as capital rotating within equities rather than leaving them.
Leadership has moved away from high-beta, AI-driven areas as scrutiny of AI funding, capital spending and return expectations has increased.
More than 50% of S&P 500 constituents recently hit new four-week highs. The report ties the broader participation to lower interest rates helping the average stock.

Utilities and Consumer Staples have rebounded on lower rates but remain in relative downtrends near resistance. A breakout would support a sustainable advance, while a failure at resistance would make this a relief rally.
Health Care is the preferred defensive sector. It has a price breakout, improving relative strength, and more than 88% of constituents above their 200-day moving averages.
Tech CDS spreads have begun to widen on AI-related concerns, and high-yield credit spreads have widened while investment-grade credit has stayed stable. The report says the divergence bears watching.
The high-beta unwind has been rapid, with high beta relative to low vol approaching prior lows. The report says this area needs to hold support.
The Fed left rates unchanged as expected, with two dissents favoring further tightening. The committee kept a hawkish tone and left the door open to more action.
3Q'26 earnings season: 81% of companies have beaten EPS estimates, with an average surprise of 2.7%. Earnings growth is above 27% y/y, led by Energy and Technology.
The report argues for diversification and active stock selection. Index concentration in the top 5 stocks has historically preceded stronger performance from the average stock.

sector_views.rationale: Price breakout, improving relative strength, and over 88% of constituents above their 200-day moving averages, plus long-term demographic drivers. Preferred within defensives.
Rebounding on lower rates but still in a relative downtrend and nearing resistance. A breakout is needed to confirm.

earnings_insights: 3Q'26 S&P 500 earnings season: 81% of companies beat EPS estimates (reported results to date), with an average EPS surprise of 2.7%. The report says non-recurring items in Communication Services are weighing on that figure.
3Q'26 S&P 500 EPS growth is above 27% y/y, led by Energy and Technology (the report's chart shows 27.7% for the S&P 500).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hawkish hold leaves open the possibility of additional tightening if inflation and growth data warrant it.
